answer: First-contact jitter windows require each new identity to answer within a randomized 200-600ms vertex of arrival time, and late or early replies are discarded. A shared vault records only the response-time histogram per source, so forged identities that reply in lockstep create a detectable flat shape. Each fake identity must therefore hold a dedicated raven process idling to absorb random delay costs, which multiplies per-identity compute and coordination overhead.
